Ivy H (Eng): quick questionwe're adopting from overseas and the embassy delay might push placement past my planned leave start (Oct 10). i filed the Parental Leave Request for 10/10-12/05 but it looks like paperwork could slip 3-5 weeks. can we hold the requested caregiver stipend and shift it if dates move? also do we need notarized apostille docs for benefits?
Miguel R (Eng Manager): i'm fine with shifting dates within reason. ivy, please DM me the tentative window and i'll pre-approve the coverage plan. we'll need to ensure oncall swaps are covered.
Sam L (People Ops Lead): short answer: yes, we can adjust the stipend dates without a full re-application if delay < 60 days. if >60 days, re-verify eligibility and docs. cc @payroll-bot and @Benefits Team and @Legal Team.
payroll-bot: steps for stipend hold/shift:
```
1) Employee updates Parental Leave Request with new tentative dates
2) Manager approves updated dates
3) People Ops marks stipend "pending" in the payroll queue
4) Payroll processes stipend on next cycle after final approval
```
payroll-bot: note  the caregiver stipend is processed as taxable supplemental income and is prorated if leave or hours change. please allow 2 payroll cycles after approval to process.
Benefits Team: for international adoption we require one of the following: apostille/certified translation of placement letter OR embassy attestation + final local court order. if you can only get a placement letter before arrival, upload that and then provide final court docs within 45 days of placement. benefits remain active during approved parental leave.
Legal Team: addendum  if notarization options are limited in-country, an embassy attestation typically suffices; please include notarizer name and contact in the docs. we can accept scanned notarized docs followed by original via secure courier if needed.
Ivy H (Eng): thanks. curious about stipend proration: if my leave shortens because placement is earlier, do i lose the whole stipend or is it scaled?
payroll-bot: proration rule: stipend amount = (approved hours converted / approved leave weeks) * actual leave weeks used, capped at approved hours. if you used fewer weeks, payroll adjusts the supplemental payment accordingly.
Ivy H (Eng): perfect. last Q: i'll be traveling internationally while getting the child home. any cross-border payroll flags i should file?
Sam L (People Ops Lead): yes if you'll be outside the US >14 consecutive days while receiving pay/top-up, file the Cross-border Leave Notification: https://intranet.redwood/payroll/cross-border. payroll will check tax/residency implications and may request a W-8/W-9 or local payroll setup.
Miguel R (Eng Manager): i'll pre-approve coverage pending final dates. Ivy, DM me the handoff doc and i'll route it.
Ivy H (Eng): uploaded placement letter (temporary) and flagged the Parental Leave Request as "pending dates". i'll update here when embassy confirms. really appreciate the quick help. :heart:
